Round 2. RabbitMQ confirms: manual-ack deliveries "not acked" are "automatically requeued" on channel/connection close; "Positive acknowledgements simply instruct RabbitMQ to record a message as delivered and can be discarded" (so ack-first then stop loses it). OutboxRelay.RelayDueAsync sets PublishedAt after PublishAsync, commits in finally ("A crash after a confirm and before the commit publishes that row again"); ClaimDueAsync selects only `WHERE published_at IS NULL`, so recording it first then stopping never publishes the row.

refs/efcore-docs transactions.md:17: "By default, if the database provider supports transactions, all changes in a single call to `SaveChanges` are applied in a transaction. If any of the changes fail, then the transaction is rolled back and none of the changes are applied to the database." HandleAsync opens no explicit transaction, so the default applies.

PG 17 ddl-constraints: a primary key "requires that the values be both unique and not null"; indexes-unique: "When an index is declared unique, multiple table rows with equal indexed values are not allowed." errcodes-appendix: `23505 unique_violation`. tutorial-transactions: "a transaction block that was put in aborted state by the system due to an error". Migration InitialCreate: PrimaryKey("PK_inbox_messages", x => x.message_id).

stage-3 DonHang.Messaging/Inbox.cs: `ex.InnerException is PostgresException { SqlState: PostgresErrorCodes.UniqueViolation } postgres && postgres.ConstraintName == "PK_inbox_messages"`. Constraint name matches DonHang.Notifications/Migrations/20261005232044_InitialCreate.cs `table.PrimaryKey("PK_inbox_messages", x => x.message_id)`.

OrderEventsConsumer.OnReceivedAsync (subscribed via `consumer.ReceivedAsync += (_, delivery) => OnReceivedAsync(channel, delivery)`): `await HandleAsync(...); await channel.BasicAckAsync(delivery.DeliveryTag, multiple: false);` inside try; `catch (PoisonMessageException)` -> BasicRejectAsync(requeue: false); `catch (Exception)` -> BasicNackAsync(requeue: true). No ack on any exception path. Supports §5 naming OnReceivedAsync as the method that acknowledges.

Execution: outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/duplicate-message.txt shows both publishes with one id print `routed: true`.

stage-3 OrderEventsConsumer.SubjectFor: "order.placed" => "order placed", "order.cancelled", "order.shipped", "order.refund-requested", "order.refunded", "order.refund-failed"; default throws PoisonMessageException. Six keys, three of them refund keys, as the lesson says.

OrderEventsConsumer only adds rows (NewEmail sets Status = "pending"); no IEmailSender use. NotificationSender.SendOneAsync: `await email.SendAsync(...)` then `notification.Status = "sent"`, saved later in queue.CompleteAsync; comment: "(1) send the email, (2) mark the row sent, (3) save it in CompleteAsync ... at least once, never lost."

scripts/backend/duplicate-message.sh: publish() posts `routing_key: "order.shipped"`, orderId 2, `properties: {message_id: $id, delivery_mode: 2}` to `http://rabbitmq:15672/api/exchanges/%2F/donhang.orders/publish`, prints `routed: \(.routed)`; called twice with one $message_id; `sleep 2`; lists notifications since $started; counts inbox_messages with that id. Comment: "as OutboxRelay would send it" supports §7's reworded "straight to RabbitMQ, the way the relay would".

Captured output at the tag, outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/duplicate-message.txt: "  routed: true" twice, then under email jobs "2 | order shipped" (one line), then under inbox_messages count "1". Matches the lesson's expected result exactly.

Lesson wording (§4) is conditional on the setup, not a ranking: ids kept in Redis make "two separate writes". EF Core transaction covers "all changes in a single call to SaveChanges" on one database connection (refs/efcore-docs transactions.md:17); a Redis write is outside it, so either write order leaves a crash window (id-first loses, effect-first repeats). Supported as written.
